item.title: Critical Citrix NetScaler auth bypass now leveraged in attacks
item.description: Actively exploited auth bypass in NetScaler ADC/Gateway lets attackers skip login entirely -- patch or take internet-facing appliances offline now.

item.title: Critical VMware Workstation and Fusion Flaw Lets VM Admins Execute Host Code
item.description: A guest VM can break out and run code on the host, undermining the isolation VM admins rely on for untrusted workloads.

item.title: Attackers Breached JetBrains Cadence via Unpatched TeamCity, Extracting AWS Credentials
item.description: An unpatched TeamCity server let attackers pivot into AWS credentials -- a reminder that CI/CD systems are high-value supply-chain targets.

item.title: Go grandmaster becomes first human to win series against advanced AI engine in 3-hour match
item.description: A human beat a top AI engine at Go for the first time in years, pushing back on the narrative that AI has permanently surpassed humans at the game.

item.title: No Law was one of the most exciting games I saw at Gamescom: a cyberpunk immersive sim that solves one of Deus Ex's biggest problems
item.description: A Gamescom preview standout that reportedly fixes one of the immersive-sim genre's long-standing design problems with a more systemic, player-driven approach.

item.title: Breaking through AlphaFold's limits to predict how proteins change shape
item.description: **Problem:** AlphaFold3 normally predicts one static protein shape, but many proteins work by flipping between multiple shapes -- a blind spot for drug design. **Approach:** researchers added a "repulsive force" to AlphaFold3's diffusion model: each new prediction is penalized for landing too close to a shape it already generated, pushing it toward different ones. **Result:** the tweaked model (AF3-ReD) found open, closed, and intermediate shapes of an ATP synthase subunit; stock AlphaFold3 only ever found the open one. **Why it matters:** drugs often target one specific shape of a protein -- seeing all the shapes makes design far more precise. **Glossary:** diffusion model (AI that generates by refining noise into structure); conformation (a molecule's 3D shape); ATP synthase (enzyme that makes cellular energy); bias energy (a penalty term steering predictions).

item.title: Medieval manuscripts are "biological time capsules" for deadly sheeppox virus
item.description: Ancient parchment made from animal skin preserved viral DNA for centuries, giving researchers a genetic timeline of a livestock pathogen.

item.title: Running Generative AI on an RP2350
item.description: **Problem:** running image-generating AI usually needs a GPU and cloud servers -- the opposite of cheap, private, offline hardware. **Approach:** a hobbyist squeezed a diffusion transformer (the architecture family behind modern image generators) onto an RP2350, a sub-$1 microcontroller, by shrinking the model to 8-bit numbers so it fits in 4MB of flash. **Result:** the chip generates recognizable 128x128 human faces in about 20 seconds each, shown over USB or VGA. **Why it matters:** it shows current AI image techniques scale down to bare-metal hardware, opening the door to private, offline AI features in cheap embedded devices instead of cloud APIs. **Glossary:** microcontroller (a tiny low-power computer chip); diffusion transformer (a neural network that generates images by denoising); quantization (shrinking number precision to save memory); VAE (variational auto-encoder, compresses images into a compact code).

item.title: Trusting-Trust Attack against an Entire Linux Distribution (via the strip utility)
item.description: A working reproduction of Ken Thompson's classic compiler-backdoor idea, scaled to compromise an entire Linux distro via the strip utility -- a stark reminder that toolchain trust is fragile.

item.title: M2: Episode 1 (or, Asahi Linux on M3)
item.description: Continued reverse-engineering progress bringing Linux support to Apple's M-series silicon, this time tackling the M3.
